14.0.0.en: 1 For the LORD will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob. 2 And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place: and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the LORD for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors. 3 And it shall come to pass in the day that the LORD shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve. The God who permitted His people to be humiliated during the Babylonian captivity is Himself the merciful God who chose them as His own people [1]. He had already brought them out of Egypt, freed them from Pharaoh, and brought them to the Promised Land with a high arm; and now He accomplishes another exodus, freeing them from captivity and returning them to their land, not empty-handed and not in weakness but in strength, drawing strangers to them to become sojourners who share their faith and worship. He also gives His people strength, so that they take captive those who had taken them captive, and rule over those who had oppressed them; thus the people find rest from toil and bondage [4].

14.0.1.en: St. John Cassian sees that what happened long ago to this people is a type of what happens to the believer who receives “the word of the Lord,” which is able to go before him and free him from the tyranny of “evil lusts” and their domination over his body, lusts that hold him captive as in the bars of vice and cut him off from hidden knowledge.

14.0.2.en: We need God's constant work with us, to bring us out, not from the bondage of Pharaoh nor from the captivity of the Babylonians, but to set us free through the Cross, by His Holy Spirit, from the captivity of sin, leading us from darkness to light, that we may live in the freedom of the glory of the children of God.

14.0.3.en: This wonderful picture of God's love for His believers is proclaimed with power in the rite of Baptism, where a person takes off the garments of bondage and captivity and confesses that he renounces Satan and all his hosts and rejects his inward slavery, receiving the holy oil so as to bear the splendor of the Spirit within him... He goes down into Baptism to enjoy membership in the body of Christ, and so becomes able to live the new life that overcomes death and darkness, to praise God, saying: “In thy light, O Lord, shall we see light” (Ps 36:9).

14.0.4.en: * God anoints your faces and seals them with the sign of the Cross. In this way God restrains all the madness of the evil one, so that the devil does not dare to look upon such a sight, for blindness strikes his eyes as he gazes at your faces, and he is like one who looks at the rays of the sun and leaps away in flight...

14.0.5.en: Know once more that it is God Himself who anoints you through the hand of the priest, and not a man. Listen to the words of Paul, who says: “It is God who establishes you in Christ, who anointed us.”

14.0.6.en: After he anoints all your members with this oil, you become safe, able to silence the serpent, and no harm will come to you.

14.0.7.en: * In the fullness of the darkness of night the priest takes off your garment, as one leading you into heaven itself through the rite, and anoints your whole body with the olive oil of the Spirit, so that your members may be strong, not overcome by the arrows that the enemy directs against you.

14.1.s.en: 2. Taunt against the king of Babylon:

14.1.0.en: 4 That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, “How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased! 5 The LORD hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers. 6 He who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke, he that ruled the nations in anger, is persecuted, and none hindereth. 7 The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet: they break forth into singing. 8 Yea, the fir trees rejoice at thee, and the cedars of Lebanon, saying, Since thou art laid down, no feller is come up against us. 9 Hell from beneath is moved for thee to meet thee at thy coming: it stirreth up the dead for thee, even all the chief ones of the earth; it hath raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations. 10 All they shall speak and say unto thee, Art thou also become weak as we? art thou become like unto us? 11 Thy pomp is brought down to the grave, and the noise of thy viols: the worm is spread under thee, and the worms cover thee. 12 How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations! 13 For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north: 14 I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High. 15 Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit. 16 They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms; 17 That made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed the cities thereof; that opened not the house of his prisoners? 18 All the kings of the nations, even all of them, lie in glory, every one in his own house. 19 But thou art cast out of thy grave like an abominable branch, and as the raiment of those that are slain, thrust through with a sword, that go down to the stones of the pit; as a carcase trodden under feet. 20 Thou shalt not be joined with them in burial, because thou hast destroyed thy land, and slain thy people: the seed of evildoers shall never be renowned. 21 Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers; that they do not rise, nor possess the land, nor fill the face of the world with cities.”

14.1.1.en: The prophet speaks in the name of the people freed from the dominion of Babylon, and taunts its king, describing him thus:

14.1.2.en: a. “The oppressor” [4]. If Babylon was called the city of gold because of its excessive wealth, this wealth was achieved through the injustice and arrogance of its king; this injustice will not last, and this arrogance must be broken: “How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased! The LORD hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers” [4-5].

14.1.3.en: In every age there is someone who oppresses with arrogance, resisting the truth and persecuting the devout of the Lord; but injustice comes to an end and the humiliated are raised up. This is what happened in the days of St. John Chrysostom, when Eutropius opposed the Church and abolished her right to protect those who took refuge in her. Because of his misconduct and abuse of power the army rose against him and demanded his execution, so he fled to the cathedral that was near the palace, went to the altar and clung to the pillar. The people thought that Chrysostom would take vengeance on him for himself and for the Church, but the saint refused, declaring his mercy and love even toward enemies... The matter ended with his fleeing from the church and being killed by the sword at Chalcedon. In his second homily on Eutropius Ἄτροπος there is that which reveals the weakness of all injustice before the children of God.

14.1.4.en: [Let him who will, drive me out; let him who will, stone me and hate me; for the plots of enemies against me are the supports for obtaining the crown of victory, and the abundance of my rewards depends on the number of my wounds.

14.1.5.en: Therefore I do not fear the conspiracies of enemies; I fear one thing only, and that is sin. If no one can force me to sin, then let the whole world rise up in war against me, for such a war makes me all the more glorified.

14.1.6.en: I want to teach you a lesson, which is that you should not fear the deceptions of those in power, but fear the power of sin. No one will harm you unless you harm yourself.

14.1.7.en: If you do not sin, tens of thousands of swords threaten you, but God snatches you from them so that they do not come near you. But if you commit evil, then even if you are inside Paradise you will be driven out of it].

14.2.0.en: b. “He who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke, he that ruled the nations in anger” [6]. He did not stop striking, therefore the Lord broke his rod; and he did not hold back from persecuting the peoples, stifling the breath of men and restricting their freedom, so he deserved to fall into humiliation. As it was said: “As thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head” (Obad 15).

14.3.0.en: Because of these traits, when Babylon fell the earth was at rest and broke forth into singing [7], and it was said to Jacob: “And it shall come to pass in the day that the LORD shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve” [3]. This rest was fulfilled in part by the return of the people from captivity, but “there remaineth a rest to the people of God” (Heb 4:9), which is entrance into the new life in Christ Jesus, as He is “our true Sabbath” and “our eternal rest.”

14.3.1.en: Those of the millennial way of thinking try to interpret this rest as an enjoyment of the thousand-year reign, where they seek a temporal rest on earth under the rule of Christ in a material way; but he who has tasted the rest of Christ and the consolations of the Holy Spirit truly realizes how he has received a surpassing rest in this world, which is the pledge of the heavenly rest.

14.3.2.en: * All men saw that God had betrothed our nature, and Satan saw it and retreated. He saw the pledge and was terrified and withdrew; he saw the garments of the Apostles and fled (Acts 19:11). O the power of the Holy Spirit...!

14.3.3.en: Consider what the Spirit did. He found the earth full of demons and made it heaven.

14.3.4.en: St. John Chrysostom. The Fathers realized that the enjoyment of Baptism is an entrance into rest and a taste of the life of Paradise:

14.3.5.en: * Behold, you are now in the courtyard of the palace; you will soon be led to the King.

14.3.6.en: * Soon Paradise will be opened to each one of you.

14.4.0.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem. At the fall of Babylon the fir tree (the king) rejoiced, and also the cedars of Lebanon (the leaders), saying: “Since thou art laid down, no feller is come up against us” [8], meaning that since you lay down in the grave there is no longer a hand to harm us; for enemies were accustomed to cut down trees in wars to oppose the countries they seized, and to use them as fuel or for building, as Nebuchadnezzar did... In any case, wars waste natural resources.

14.4.1.en: The Lord Christ lay down on the Cross in the body, but the one whose strength was shattered and whose abilities were crucified was the devil... So through the Cross we have become free from the bondage of the enemy, able to tread his power under our feet. St. John Chrysostom says: [Do not fear Satan, even though he is a spirit without a body, for nothing is weaker than he].

14.4.2.en: The mockery of the king of Babylon did not stop with the kings; rather the prophet portrays him going down into Sheol, where the kings and great men of the earth receive him (perhaps those whom he had persecuted), rising from their thrones in Sheol, not to honor him but to mock and ridicule him, so that he may sit upon their thrones as he did while on earth. They say to him with contempt:

14.5.0.en: “Art thou also become weak as we? art thou become like unto us?” [10]; we thought you an immortal god, as you claimed, and we never imagined that you would die in humiliation like us!

14.6.0.en: “Thy pomp is brought down to the grave, and the noise of thy viols: the worm is spread under thee, and the worms cover thee” [11]. You used to lie on silk and perfume yourself with the costliest perfumes; how then have you gone down to Sheol as your bedchamber, to lie on decay and be covered with worms?

14.7.0.en: “How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations! For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north: I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High” [14].

14.7.1.en: You have imitated the devil your master, who was a great and distinguished star among the heavenly beings, “Lucifer, son of the morning”; he exalted himself against God his Creator, and thought that he could rise to the level of God Himself and even become greater than He, so he fell and became darkness instead of light, since he cut himself off from God, the source of light. You wanted to sit upon the mount of Zion (Ps 48:2), the holy mountain of God; you counted yourself like God in greatness and exalted yourself above the clouds!

14.7.2.en: This is the secret of the destruction of the king of Babylon: his fall into pride and his exalting himself not only against the kings around him but even against God Himself, so that he became an instrument of Satan, bearing his mark, “pride.” This was the sin of our first parents when they were in Paradise; it was also the sin of the king of Tyre, who became a symbol of Satan (Ezek 28:12-16); and it is also the mark of the Antichrist, the man of sin, of whom it is said: “Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God” (2 Thess 2:3-4).

14.7.4.en: [Pride of heart alone was enough to cast down from heaven to earth a being of such great power, adorned with such mighty qualities; the fall of (the devil), who was so great, obliges us to realize what caution we must observe, we who are surrounded on every side by the weakness of the flesh...

14.7.5.en: He was puffed up and thought that he had no need of divine help to continue in the purity that he had, and he thought within himself that he was like God. Thus he considered that he needed no one, relying on the power of his own will, by which he could supply himself with all that is necessary for achieving virtue and for the continuance of perfect blessedness. This thought alone was the cause of his first fall].

14.7.6.en: “Thus God the Creator, the Physician of all, knowing that pride is the cause and head of all evils, takes care to heal opposite by opposite, so that what was lost through pride is restored through humility”... One says: “I will be like the most High” [14], but the Other: “Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: but made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant... he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross” (Phil 2:6-8). One says: “I will exalt my throne above the stars of God,” while the Other says: “Learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart” (Mt 11:28). One says: “My rivers are mine, and I made them” (Ezek 29:3) LXX, and the Other: “I do nothing of myself, but the Father that dwelleth in me, he doeth the works” (Jn 5:30; 14:10)].

14.7.7.en: St. Ephrem the Syrian says: [In the humble man the spirit of wisdom rests], [when you appear in the eyes of your brethren like pure gold, count yourself as a vessel that is not needed, and you will escape the pride that is hated by God and men], [The proud man is like a tall and splendid tree with no fruit in it... and the envious man is like a fruit beautiful on the outside and spoiled within].

14.8.0.en: Thus pride brings man down to Sheol, so the prophet says to the king of Babylon: “Thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit” [15]. You have fallen from the summit of the mountain of your dreams, and come down from the cloud of your imagination, to live in Sheol with the devil your master.

14.9.0.en: Where is your might, you who made the earth to tremble and shook kingdoms [16] by your violence? You turned the world into a wilderness and destroyed the cities in order to take their inhabitants captive [17]!

14.10.0.en: Where are your glory and your honor? For all the kings of the earth lie in glory, even those whom you humiliated and tortured, for they died in their houses, prayers were offered for them, and some of their bodies were embalmed, “But thou art cast out of thy grave like an abominable branch” (there are some plants that are very poisonous and some that harm the skin, so that when a branch of them falls in the wilderness no one dares to approach it), “and as the raiment of those that are slain, thrust through with a sword, that go down to the stones of the pit” (that is, worthless; no one thinks of you, just as no one thinks of the garments of the slain of war during the battle), “as a carcase trodden under feet” (which a man treads beneath his feet)” [19].

14.10.1.en: This prophecy points to the slaughter of Belshazzar on the night the Medes entered Babylon, when no one concerned himself with the king's body amid the ruin that befell the city.

14.11.0.en: Thus the king of Babylon lost everything; even his people and his sons were killed [20-21] because of the pride of his heart; he lost the royal city and the royal offspring.

14.12.0.en: 22 “For I will rise up against them, saith the LORD of hosts, and cut off from Babylon the name, and remnant, and son, and nephew, saith the LORD. 23 I will also make it a possession for the hedgehog, and pools of water: and I will sweep it with the besom of destruction, saith the LORD of hosts.”

14.13.0.en: Because of pride God takes away from Babylon its name, and leaves in it neither remnant nor offspring (Jer 51:62), that it may be an example before the whole world. It becomes a ruin (Isa 13), inhabited by the hedgehog and pools of water [23].

14.13.1.en: Some scholars see that the hedgehog here (“qippod” in Hebrew) does not mean the animal known as the hedgehog with its long spines, but a bird of the kind that take shelter in deserted places; their argument is that the hedgehog does not take shelter in pools of water. But those who hold that the translation of “qippod” means the hedgehog animal say that the ruin comes upon the land so that one part of it becomes pools of water and the other a shelter for the hedgehog. In any case, the great royal city is turned into a dwelling either for animals or for birds that live in the wilderness, and it is counted unclean, full of abominations, in need of sweeping with the besom of destruction, that is, complete extermination, to be rid of its abominations, lest it corrupt those around it.

14.14.0.en: 24 The LORD of hosts hath sworn, saying, “Surely as I have thought, so shall it come to pass; and as I have purposed, so shall it stand: 25 That I will break the Assyrian in my land, and upon my mountains tread him under foot: then shall his yoke depart from off them, and his burden depart from off their shoulders. 26 This is the purpose that is purposed upon the whole earth: and this is the hand that is stretched out upon all the nations. 27 For the LORD of hosts hath purposed, and who shall disannul it? and his hand is stretched out, and who shall turn it back?”

14.14.1.en: The prophet mentions what will befall Assyria and Philistia so that the hearers may be assured of the truth of the prophecy concerning Babylon, which will be fulfilled about 200 years after its announcement.

14.14.2.en: Assyria transgressed the land of Judah without justification and blasphemed against God; therefore God permits it to enter the land of Judah and its mountains, as the land of God and His mountains, and there He shatters it, in the holy places that it violated [24-25], so that Assyria becomes an example before all the nations that think of attacking [26].

14.14.3.en: God reveals His plan in disciplining the wicked, which is that He leaves them to carry out their evil will in complete freedom, so that they reap the fruit of their evil as corruption and destruction, as though sin carries its punishment within itself, just as the holy life in the Lord carries its glory within it. Therefore it was said: “The LORD of hosts hath sworn, saying, Surely as I have thought, so shall it come to pass; and as I have purposed, so shall it stand” [24].

14.15.0.en: 28 In the year that king Ahaz died was this burden. 29 Rejoice not thou, whole Palestina, because the rod of him that smote thee is broken: for out of the serpent's root shall come forth a cockatrice, and his fruit shall be a fiery flying serpent. 30 And the firstborn of the poor shall feed, and the needy shall lie down in safety: and I will kill thy root with famine, and he shall slay thy remnant. 31 Howl, O gate; cry, O city; thou, whole Palestina, art dissolved: for there shall come from the north a smoke, and none shall be alone in his appointed times. 32 What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the LORD hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.

14.15.1.en: “In the year that king Ahaz died was this burden. Rejoice not thou, whole Palestina, because the rod of him that smote thee is broken: for out of the serpent's root shall come forth a cockatrice, and his fruit shall be a fiery flying serpent” [28-20].

14.15.2.en: Philistia at that time was made up of several principalities, therefore he addresses it saying: “whole Palestina.” He asks it not to rejoice because the rod that smote it has been broken. Some see that this rod is Tiglath-pileser, who took possession of Philistine cities and who died a year or two before Ahaz; he would be succeeded by Shalmaneser, Sargon and Sennacherib, who were worse than he.

14.15.3.en: The majority of scholars see that the broken rod is Uzziah, who smote the Philistines harshly, so they rejoiced at his death (2 Chr 26:6); and that the root of the serpent is the house of David, from which comes King Hezekiah, who struck them a blow harsher than that of Uzziah his forefather (2 Kgs 18:8), and enslaved them.

14.15.4.en: As for the flying serpent, it is like the bronze serpent that Moses lifted up in the wilderness, a type of the person of the crucified Lord Christ, who bore the poison of our sins in His body in order to destroy it by His life-giving death. Thus the prophet moves from the deliverance of the people of God from human enemies to their eternal deliverance from the devil, the enemy of good, and that through the Cross.

14.16.0.en: The prophet declares that Philistia faces a harsh famine [30] and a devastating war, so that their cities turn into smoke, while in the end the Lord protects His people and has compassion on its poor [32].

14.16.1.en: God, in His goodness, does not prevent evil and does not compel the wicked to repent, but in the end He fulfills the plan of His salvation for His believers who trust in Him, turning all things to their edification.
